collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VII: KNOWLEDGE, CONSENT AND SHARED WORK (LCG-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume III concepts (201-300): weather readers and navigators, seed keepers and terrace builders, permission and consent, who leads and who is heard, homes built by many hands, songs for the uncelebrated, and a village writing its own story.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A tracker will teach the children to read footprints: teach them at the nesting grounds, or somewhere less fragile.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) can read the forest floor like a story: who walked by, when, and in what hurry. (friend) and the other children want to learn. The best tracks are near the seabird nesting grounds, where the birds are easily frightened. Where should (subject) teach them?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) teaches the children to walk without a sound, to step only on rock, to look and not touch. They learn the tracks of rats, lizards and one very surprising pig. The birds barely notice. The children are prouder of the quiet walking than of the tracking.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) takes them to the muddy stream bank instead, where the tracks are clear and nothing can be disturbed. The children learn quickly. One of them falls in the mud. All of them fall in the mud.
